pairings.priority_text: The exemption was written in 1967 for a bank stuck with a building it never wanted, and for decades it mostly covered homes. Then investors learned to buy the loan instead of the building, and the Assessor now counts $450M in foreclosure exemptions claimed in the last three years, against $50M in the fifteen years before that. The tax they skip is the one every ordinary buyer pays, and homes and small buildings keep the exemption either way.
